correctness.rationale: For all real a>b>0 and n>=3, an affine circle transformation and vertex-moving argument characterize all area maxima. Chord lengths reduce to a q-point square-root cosine sum. The proven Chebyshev root product yields a resolvent; the derivative is a strictly negative integral because z>1 and Tq,Tq prime are positive. A second derivative gives strict concavity. An exact positive factorization of the maximum deficit yields optimal two-sided coefficients. The integral differentiation is justified by O(s^(1/2)) at zero and O(s^(-q-1/2)) at infinity. verify.py executed successfully with 6,732 finite checks, which do not substitute for the proof.

value.rationale: Every ellipse and polygon order has a continuum of area-maximizing orientations. Euclidean perimeter is an independent natural selector, and its exact strict ordering, complete extrema, all-aspect-ratio proof and globally optimal quantitative angle stability resolve this genuine geometry degeneracy. The result is not a routine area identity, isolated computation or unsupported small numerical gain; the trigonometric resolvent yields a uniform structural theorem.
